description: After the October 2025 recapitalisation, Microsoft holds about 27% of OpenAI Group PBC on a diluted basis, a stake the companies valued at about $135 billion.
notes: Amount is a stake valuation, not cash invested. Reciprocal with a-002 (Azure commitment) and a-003 (revenue share). Microsoft FY2026 results (29 Jul 2026) excluded a $4.963B after-tax OpenAI gain from non-GAAP figures.

description: As part of the recapitalisation, OpenAI contracted to buy an incremental $250 billion of Azure services; Microsoft gave up its right of first refusal on OpenAI compute.
notes: No term disclosed. Reciprocal with a-001. April 2026 amendment removed Azure exclusivity for OpenAI products. A secondary analysis of the FY2026 10-K reports OpenAI supplied about $24.1B (7.3%) of Microsoft FY2026 revenue; that figure was not checked against the filing.

description: Under the April 2026 amendment OpenAI keeps paying Microsoft a revenue share through 2030, subject to a cap that press reports put at $38 billion in total.
source_publisher: Reuters (via Yahoo Finance), citing The Information
notes: Cap amount is a media report (The Information); Reuters could not verify it. The companies confirmed only that a cap exists. The 20% rate is from the FT, citing one person. Microsoft no longer pays OpenAI a revenue share.

description: OpenAI agreed to buy about $300 billion of Oracle cloud compute over roughly five years from 2027, tied to 4.5 GW of Stargate capacity.
notes: The $300B figure is from WSJ reporting; Oracle did not publish the contract value. Oracle RPO was $455B at Q1 FY2026 and $664B at Q1 FY2027 (10 Sep 2026); Oracle does not break out the OpenAI share. A planned 600 MW Abilene expansion was reported dropped in March 2026; Oracle disputes that the wider build is off track.

description: The Financial Times reported that Oracle would buy about $40 billion of Nvidia GB200 chips (about 400,000 units) for the OpenAI Stargate site in Abilene, Texas.
source_publisher: Reuters (via AOL), citing the Financial Times
notes: Media report; neither company confirmed the amount. The chips serve the OpenAI contract in a-004.

description: SoftBank Vision Fund 2 invested an aggregate $34.6 billion in OpenAI between September 2024 and the end of 2025, before the 2026 follow-on.
notes: Cumulative figure stated by SoftBank when it announced the follow-on in a-007.

description: SoftBank completed a $30 billion follow-on investment in OpenAI in three $10 billion tranches (April, July, October 2026), which lifted its cumulative investment to $64.6 billion and its stake to about 13%.
notes: Priced at a $730B pre-money valuation. Financed first with a $40B bridge facility (March 2026), later repaid; the last tranche was funded from senior notes. Part of the $122B OpenAI round.

description: Amazon committed up to $50 billion to OpenAI in the February 2026 round: $15 billion up front and $35 billion that depends on later conditions.
notes: The realized amount is the up-front tranche as reported in coverage; the conditions for the remaining $35B (reported as an IPO or an AGI milestone) come from The Information. Reciprocal with a-009 and a-010 (OpenAI spend on AWS).

description: OpenAI signed a seven-year, $38 billion agreement to use AWS infrastructure built on Nvidia GB200 and GB300 systems.
notes: Expanded in February 2026; see a-010.

description: OpenAI and AWS expanded the $38 billion agreement by $100 billion over eight years, with OpenAI committing to use about 2 GW of Trainium capacity.
notes: Incremental to a-009. Reciprocal with a-008 (Amazon equity investment announced the same day).

description: Nvidia committed $30 billion to the OpenAI round that closed in March 2026 at an $852 billion post-money valuation.
notes: This replaced the September 2025 LOI in a-012. Reports differ on whether the money was paid at once or in three instalments. The Nvidia 10-Q does not name OpenAI; it shows non-marketable equity additions of about $31B in the first half of fiscal 2027. Reciprocal with a-013 and a-014.

description: In September 2025 Nvidia signed a letter of intent to invest up to $100 billion in OpenAI progressively as 10 GW of Nvidia systems were deployed.
notes: Non-binding LOI; no definitive agreement was signed. In February 2026 Jensen Huang said it was never a commitment. Effectively superseded by the $30B investment in a-011. Do not add to a-011.

description: Under the September 2025 letter of intent OpenAI planned to deploy at least 10 GW of Nvidia systems, with the first gigawatt on Vera Rubin in the second half of 2026.
notes: Non-binding LOI. Reciprocal with a-012. No purchase value disclosed.

description: With the February 2026 round, OpenAI committed to use 3 GW of dedicated inference capacity and 2 GW of training capacity on Nvidia Vera Rubin systems.
notes: Reciprocal with a-011 (Nvidia $30B investment). No dollar value disclosed.

description: OpenAI agreed to deploy 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs over several generations, starting with 1 GW of MI450 in the second half of 2026.
notes: No contract value disclosed; AMD described expected revenue as tens of billions of dollars. Reciprocal with a-016 (warrant). No 2026 confirmation of first-tranche vesting was found.

description: AMD issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares at $0.01 each, which vests as OpenAI deploys AMD GPUs and as AMD share-price targets are met.
notes: Supplier gives equity to its customer: value flows from AMD to OpenAI. Reciprocal with a-015. Final tranche needs an AMD share price of $600. Up to about 10% of AMD if fully exercised.

description: OpenAI and Broadcom agreed to co-develop and deploy 10 GW of OpenAI-designed custom accelerators and Broadcom networking, with racks from late 2026 through 2029.
notes: Financial terms not disclosed. No 2026 status update was found.

description: CoreWeave contracts with OpenAI total up to about $22.4 billion after a third agreement of up to $6.5 billion in September 2025.
notes: Sum of up to $11.9B (March 2025), up to $4B (May 2025) and up to $6.5B (September 2025). All are ceilings.

description: OpenAI signed a multi-year agreement for 750 MW of Cerebras inference capacity through 2028, valued at more than $10 billion at signing.
notes: OpenAI gave no value; the $10B+ figure is from press reports. Coverage of the Cerebras S-1 says the agreement is worth more than $20B at full expansion to 2 GW by 2030. S-1 coverage also describes a $1B OpenAI loan to Cerebras and an OpenAI warrant over Cerebras shares; those terms were not verified here.

description: The Information reported that SoftBank would commit $19 billion of equity to the Stargate venture for a 40% share.
notes: Media report, not confirmed. The Stargate headline is up to $500B over four years with Oracle and MGX as further equity partners; that headline is not an edge. See a-021.

description: The Information reported that OpenAI would commit $19 billion of equity to the Stargate venture for a 40% share.
notes: Media report, not confirmed. Pair of a-020.

description: Disney agreed to make a $1 billion equity investment in OpenAI and receive warrants, together with a three-year character licence for Sora.
notes: Subject to definitive agreements and approvals at announcement; closing was not verified. Disney also becomes an OpenAI API customer (no value disclosed).

description: Samsung signed a letter of intent to supply memory for Stargate; OpenAI targets up to 900,000 DRAM wafer starts a month across Samsung and SK hynix.
notes: Non-binding LOI; no value or schedule disclosed. The 900,000 figure is a joint ceiling with a-024. No 2026 definitive contract was found.

description: SK hynix signed a letter of intent to supply memory for Stargate; OpenAI targets up to 900,000 DRAM wafer starts a month across Samsung and SK hynix.
notes: Non-binding LOI; no value or schedule disclosed. Pair of a-023.

target: SB Energy (lessor to an OpenAI affiliate)
description: In August 2026 Nvidia gave guarantees capped at $105 billion to support SB Energy leases for about 4.25 GW of IT load at an Ohio campus built for an affiliate of OpenAI.
notes: A guarantee (credit support), not a cash payment; maximum exposure, not expected loss. disclosure_date is the 10-Q period end; the guarantees were entered in August 2026 (subsequent event). Nvidia holds an option on about 3.8 GW more. A supplier backstops the infrastructure of its customer: see a-011 to a-014.

description: Amazon invested $8 billion in Anthropic through convertible notes between 2023 and 2025.
source_publisher: FourWeekMBA, citing the Amazon Form 10-Q for Q3 2026
notes: Secondary reading of the 10-Q filed 30 Oct 2026. Estimated fair value of the notes was $146.2B at 30 Sep 2026 (Level 3). The notes convert to non-voting Class N shares at the IPO.

description: In April 2026 Amazon agreed to invest up to $25 billion more in Anthropic: $5 billion at once and up to $20 billion tied to milestones.
notes: Realized $10B is non-voting preferred stock bought in the first nine months of 2026 per a secondary reading of the Amazon Q3 10-Q; it includes $5B in the Series H (a-041). The remaining facility (up to $15B) draws on compute-delivery milestones. Reciprocal with a-028.

description: The Anthropic S-1 shows at least $110 billion of committed AWS spend from 2026 through 2036, linked to up to 5 GW of Trainium-based capacity.
source_publisher: The Motley Fool, reporting the Anthropic Form S-1
notes: S-1 figure as reported by news outlets; the SEC document was not fetched. In April 2026 the parties announced more than $100B over ten years. Reciprocal with a-026 and a-027.

description: Google agreed in April 2026 to invest up to $40 billion in Anthropic: $10 billion in cash at a $350 billion valuation and $30 billion tied to performance targets.
notes: Realized $10B is the up-front tranche; the Series H release counts $15B of previously committed hyperscaler money (of which $5B Amazon) but does not name Google, so treat the realized figure with care. Google had invested more than $3B before this deal. Reciprocal with a-030, a-031 and a-033.

description: The Anthropic S-1 shows at least $114.5 billion of committed Google Cloud spend from 2026 through 2033, payable regardless of usage.
source_publisher: The Motley Fool, reporting the Anthropic Form S-1
notes: S-1 figure as reported by news outlets. Probably includes the October 2025 TPU deal in a-032. Reciprocal with a-029.

description: The Anthropic S-1 shows about $161.2 billion committed to Broadcom over five years for TPU-based compute capacity, non-cancellable except on default.
source_publisher: The Motley Fool, reporting the Anthropic Form S-1
notes: Largest single Anthropic commitment. The 5 GW is the joint Google and Broadcom TPU capacity named in the Series H release, with capacity from 2027. One outlet says some S-1 commitments can be cancelled after early 2027, which conflicts with the non-cancellable description. May include the orders in a-034.

description: In October 2025 Anthropic agreed to expand its use of Google Cloud to up to one million TPUs, with well over 1 GW coming online in 2026, in a deal Google described as worth tens of billions of dollars.
notes: No exact value disclosed. Likely included in the $114.5B S-1 commitment (a-030); do not add the two.

description: The S-1 says Anthropic committed to procure more TPU compute from suppliers such as Google between 2028 and 2031, at an expected cost of $125 billion to $150 billion.
source_publisher: The Motley Fool, reporting the Anthropic Form S-1
notes: Expected-cost range of $125B to $150B; the low end is recorded. Not part of the $637B of named commitments. Counterparties are described as companies such as Google.

description: Broadcom said Anthropic placed about $21 billion of orders for TPU-based systems: a $10 billion order and a later $11 billion order for delivery in late 2026.
notes: Disclosed on the Broadcom fiscal Q4 2025 earnings call; disclosure_date is the call date as recalled, check before use. Possible overlap with a-031.

description: Anthropic rents the Colossus GPU capacity of SpaceX; the Anthropic S-1 shows up to $120.5 billion through 2029, and the SpaceX filing shows a fee of $1.25 billion a month through May 2029.
source_publisher: The Motley Fool, reporting the Anthropic Form S-1
notes: Either party can cancel on 90 days' notice, so this is not a firm commitment. The SpaceX monthly fee implies about $45B for Colossus 1 alone (more than 300 MW, about 220,000 Nvidia GPUs); the larger S-1 ceiling appears to include Colossus 2. The two figures were not reconciled.

description: Anthropic committed to buy $30 billion of Azure compute in November 2025; the S-1 shows the Microsoft commitment at $44.9 billion from 2026 through 2033.
notes: The issuer release gives $30B plus an option on up to 1 GW; the $44.9B is the S-1 figure as reported by The Motley Fool. Reciprocal with a-037.

description: Microsoft committed to invest up to $5 billion in Anthropic as part of the November 2025 three-way partnership.
notes: Amount actually invested not disclosed. Microsoft reported a $3.2B gain on its Anthropic investment in Q4 FY2026, which shows that at least part was funded. Reciprocal with a-036.

description: Nvidia committed to invest up to $10 billion in Anthropic as part of the November 2025 three-way partnership.
notes: Amount actually invested not disclosed; the Nvidia 10-Q does not name Anthropic. Reciprocal with a-039.

description: Anthropic made an initial compute commitment of up to 1 GW on Nvidia Grace Blackwell and Vera Rubin systems.
notes: No value disclosed. In practice Anthropic reaches Nvidia GPUs through Azure, SpaceX, Nscale and Lambda (a-035, a-036, a-042, a-043). Reciprocal with a-038.

source: Series G investors (led by GIC and Coatue)
description: Anthropic raised a $30 billion Series G at a $380 billion post-money valuation.
notes: Co-leads included D. E. Shaw Ventures, Dragoneer, Founders Fund, ICONIQ and MGX.

source: Series H investors (led by Altimeter, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, Sequoia)
description: Anthropic raised a $65 billion Series H at a $965 billion post-money valuation.
notes: Includes $15B of previously committed hyperscaler investment, of which $5B from Amazon: overlaps a-027 and probably a-029. Do not add those to this edge.

description: Anthropic agreed to pay Nscale up to about $44.6 billion for dedicated Nvidia Vera Rubin capacity at a West Virginia campus.
source_publisher: TechCrunch, reporting the Nscale Form S-1
notes: Depends on Nscale obtaining financing; Anthropic can cancel if Nscale misses milestones. Capacity of about 460 MW is from one press report. Nvidia is an investor in Nscale (a-085).

description: Anthropic agreed to buy Nvidia GPU capacity from Lambda at a Texas data centre; the S-1 shows $41.3 billion from 2026 through 2034, and press first reported $35 billion.
source_publisher: The Motley Fool, reporting the Anthropic Form S-1
notes: Non-cancellable except in limited circumstances per the S-1 coverage. Reports say Nvidia holds the lease on the facility and Lambda is Nvidia-backed. About 350 MW per press reports.

description: Anthropic announced a $50 billion plan to build custom data centres in Texas and New York with Fluidstack.
notes: A programme figure, not a disclosed contract value with Fluidstack. Not among the seven named S-1 commitments in the coverage reviewed.

description: Anthropic signed a multi-year agreement to run Claude workloads on CoreWeave, with capacity from late 2026.
notes: Financial terms not disclosed. One unverified outlet gave $6.8B; not used.

description: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share on 18 November 2026, selling 980 million shares for about $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record.
notes: About 956.35 million of the shares were sold by Anthropic (about $79.4B gross, calculated here); the rest by selling stockholders. An underwriter option could lift the total to about $93.5B. Valuation reported at about $1.5 trillion fully diluted (Renaissance: $1.38 trillion).

description: A Reuters analysis of the IPO filing put Anthropic's 2025 distribution fees to cloud marketplace partners at about $351 million, on about $2.16 billion of sales through Amazon and Google.
notes: Reuters estimate from the confidential draft filing; not split by partner. Sales through the two partners were 47% of 2025 revenue.

description: Micron joined the Anthropic Series H as a strategic infrastructure partner.
notes: Amount not disclosed. A memory supplier invests in a buyer of memory-heavy compute. Part of a-041.

description: Samsung joined the Anthropic Series H as a strategic infrastructure partner.
notes: Amount not disclosed. Part of a-041.

description: SK hynix joined the Anthropic Series H as a strategic infrastructure partner.
notes: Amount not disclosed. Part of a-041.

description: Snowflake signed a $200 million multi-year agreement to offer Anthropic models to its customers.
notes: disclosure_date is the article date.

description: ServiceNow made Claude the preferred model family across its AI workflow products in a multi-year partnership.
notes: ServiceNow declined to give value or term. It signed a similar OpenAI deal a week earlier. No dollar values were found for Salesforce or Palantir model-provider deals.

description: Meta agreed to pay at least $10 billion over six years for Google Cloud servers and storage, according to Bloomberg.
notes: Sourced to people familiar; neither company confirmed.

description: The Information reported in February 2026 that Meta signed a multibillion-dollar deal to rent Google TPUs for model training and inference.
notes: Unconfirmed media report; no value. Talks on outright TPU purchases from 2027 were not agreed.

description: Meta bought a 49% non-voting stake in Scale AI for $14.3 billion and hired its chief executive.
notes: Amount from sources; Meta did not disclose terms. Scale said the deal valued it at $29B.

description: Meta signed a contract of up to about $14.2 billion with CoreWeave for AI compute capacity.
notes: Period and exact disclosure date as recalled from the CoreWeave filing; verify before use. Expanded in a-057.

description: Meta and CoreWeave expanded their agreement by about $21 billion for AI cloud capacity through December 2032.
notes: Incremental to a-056; Bloomberg puts total Meta contracts at CoreWeave at about $35B.

description: Meta signed an initial five-year agreement of about $3 billion with Nebius in November 2025.
notes: Disclosed with Nebius Q3 2025 results; exact day as recalled. Separate from a-059.

description: Meta agreed to buy up to $27 billion of Nebius capacity over five years: $12 billion of dedicated capacity from early 2027 and a backstop of up to $15 billion for capacity Nebius cannot sell to others.
notes: Only $12B is firm; $15B is a take-if-unsold backstop. Nvidia invested $2B in Nebius the week before (a-066).

description: Meta agreed to deploy 6 GW of AMD Instinct GPUs over several generations, with first-gigawatt shipments from the second half of 2026.
notes: Value not disclosed; press (WSJ, TechCrunch) put it at up to or above $100B. Reciprocal with a-061.

description: AMD issued Meta a performance-based warrant for up to 160 million AMD shares that vests as Meta buys AMD GPUs up to 6 GW.
notes: Same structure as the OpenAI warrant (a-016); press reports a $0.01 exercise price and a $600 share-price hurdle for the last tranche. Reciprocal with a-060.

description: Meta signed a multi-year, multi-generation agreement to buy millions of Nvidia Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips and standalone Nvidia CPUs.
notes: Financial terms not disclosed.

description: Reuters reported in September 2025 that Oracle was in talks with Meta on a multi-year cloud deal worth about $20 billion.
notes: Talks only; no signed contract was found. Keep out of totals.

description: Microsoft signed a five-year agreement with Nebius for GPU capacity in Vineland, New Jersey, worth $17.4 billion and up to $19.4 billion with options.
notes: The Nebius Form 20-F gives up to $17,392.9M through 2031 per secondary reports. In November 2026 Bloomberg reported that Microsoft tightened oversight of this project; tranches can be terminated for delivery delays.

description: Microsoft signed a five-year GPU cloud contract with IREN worth about $9.7 billion, with a 20% prepayment.
notes: IREN buys the GPUs from Dell for about $5.8B. In November 2026 Bloomberg reported a revised timeline after cabling delays at the Texas site; no cancellation.

description: Nvidia invested $2 billion in Nebius through a private placement of pre-funded warrants.
notes: disclosure_date is the article date. Reuters reported an 8.3% stake. Nebius buys Nvidia systems and sells capacity to Microsoft and Meta (a-059, a-064).

description: Microsoft signed a multibillion-dollar agreement with Lambda for tens of thousands of Nvidia GPUs.
notes: Exact value not disclosed.

description: The Nscale S-1 shows Microsoft agreements that provide for payments of up to $43.8 billion through 2033.
source_publisher: TechCrunch, reporting the Nscale Form S-1
notes: disclosure_date is the approximate S-1 filing date from press coverage. In October and November 2026, reports said Microsoft cancelled a roughly $3B UK deal with Nscale and declined to expand a Texas deal; the effect on the $43.8B figure is not clear.

description: Nvidia bought about 214.8 million Intel shares at $23.28 each for $5 billion, a stake of about 4%; the purchase closed on 26 December 2025.
notes: Announced 18 September 2025 with a product collaboration on x86 CPUs for Nvidia platforms.

description: Nvidia invested $2 billion in CoreWeave Class A shares at $87.20 a share.
notes: Adds to an existing stake. CoreWeave is a large buyer of Nvidia GPUs; see the backstop in a-071.

description: Nvidia agreed to buy CoreWeave capacity that stays unsold through April 2032, an order worth at least $6.3 billion.
notes: Disclosed in a CoreWeave SEC filing in September 2025; exact day as recalled. A demand backstop: the chip supplier guarantees revenue to its own customer. Related to a-070.

description: Nvidia agreed to invest $1 billion in Nokia at $6.01 a share, for about 2.9% of the company.
notes: Subject to closing conditions at announcement; later holdings lists show 166.4 million Nokia shares, which is consistent with completion.

description: Nvidia took part as a strategic investor in the xAI $20 billion Series E.
notes: Nvidia amount not disclosed; Bloomberg reported before closing that it planned up to $2B. xAI is a large Nvidia GPU buyer. xAI merged into SpaceX in February 2026 (a-078).

source: Series E investors (Valor, Fidelity, QIA, MGX, Nvidia, Cisco and others)
description: xAI raised an upsized $20 billion Series E in January 2026.
notes: Includes the Nvidia participation in a-073 and the Tesla investment in a-075. Earlier reports described part of the financing as debt through a special purpose vehicle.

description: Tesla agreed on 16 January 2026 to invest about $2 billion in xAI Series E preferred stock.
notes: Disclosed in the Tesla Q4 2025 shareholder letter; closing was expected in Q1 2026 and was not verified. Related-party deal.

description: Nvidia obtained a right to invest up to $2.1 billion in IREN, with a deployment of Nvidia infrastructure designs.
notes: Announced in early May 2026; disclosure_date is the article date. Structured as a warrant or right, not paid cash. IREN is a Microsoft supplier (a-065).

description: Nvidia agreed to commit up to $3.2 billion to Corning through $500 million of equity warrants and multi-year purchase agreements.
notes: Mixed equity and purchase commitment; only $500M is equity. Announced in early May 2026; disclosure_date is the article date.

description: SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026, which created a combined company valued at about $1.25 trillion.
notes: A merger of related companies, not a cash investment; the valuation is from a Bloomberg report. After the merger, SpaceX owns the Colossus data centres and rents them out (a-035, a-080).

description: SpaceX priced its IPO at $135 a share in June 2026 and raised $75 billion at a valuation of about $1.77 trillion.
notes: One outlet reports $85.7B after extra shares. The S-1 showed xAI capital expenditure of $12.7B in 2025.

description: Google agreed to pay SpaceX about $920 million a month from October 2026 through June 2029 for about 110,000 Nvidia GPUs, about $30.4 billion over the full term.
source_publisher: TechCrunch, reporting a SpaceX SEC filing
notes: Total is 33 months at $920M. Either party can cancel on 90 days' notice after 31 December 2026, so the total is not firm. Google is also a SpaceX shareholder.

description: Nvidia invested $2 billion in Synopsys common stock with a multi-year engineering partnership.
notes: Later holdings lists show about 4.8 million Synopsys shares. Exact announcement day as recalled.

description: Nvidia agreed to a deal reported at $20 billion to license Groq inference technology and hire most of its team.
notes: A licence and hiring deal, not an equity purchase; the type is the nearest fit. The Nvidia 10-Q names Groq: accrued consideration fell from $3,921M to $986M in the first half of fiscal 2027, with a $2,944M outflow. The $20B headline is a media figure.

description: Nvidia invested $2 billion in Lumentum in March 2026, with multi-billion-dollar purchase commitments for optical components.
notes: disclosure_date is the article date; the deal dates to early March 2026.

description: Nvidia invested $2 billion in Coherent in March 2026, with multi-billion-dollar purchase commitments for optical components.
notes: disclosure_date is the article date; the deal dates to early March 2026.

description: Nvidia agreed to provide $1 billion of convertible debt to Nscale as part of a $3.1 billion financing in September 2026.
notes: Other reports say Nvidia has invested more than $2B in Nscale in total. Nscale buys Nvidia GPUs and sells capacity to Microsoft and Anthropic (a-042, a-068).

description: Nvidia accounted for about 13% of TSMC revenue in the fourth quarter of 2025 and became its largest customer.
notes: TSMC filings give customer shares without names; the Nvidia identification is from press. No dollar figure recorded.

description: Apple accounted for about 11% of TSMC revenue in the fourth quarter of 2025, in second place behind Nvidia.
notes: Customer identification is from press, not from TSMC. Apple was about 24% of TSMC revenue in 2024 per press reports.

description: The largest SK hynix customer, widely identified as Nvidia, bought about 34.98 trillion won of products in January to September 2026, 14.79% of SK hynix revenue.
source_publisher: FourWeekMBA, citing the SK hynix Q3 2026 quarterly report
notes: Amount is in Korean won (about $26.1B per the source), so no USD figure is recorded. The customer is not named in the filing. The share fell from 26.98% in the same period of 2025.

description: Tesla signed a contract worth about $16.5 billion for Samsung to make its AI6 chips in Taylor, Texas, through 2033.
notes: The Samsung filing did not name the customer; Elon Musk confirmed it was Tesla.

description: Oracle will deploy an initial 50,000 AMD Instinct MI450 GPUs in a public AI supercluster from the third quarter of 2026.
notes: No value disclosed.

description: Apple and Google announced a multi-year collaboration in which the next Apple Foundation Models are based on Gemini models and Google cloud technology; press reports put the price at about $1 billion a year.
notes: The joint statement confirms the deal but gives no price. The $1B figure is a media report repeated by TechCrunch as about $1 billion; treat it as an estimate.

description: SoftBank completed its acquisition of the Arm server chip designer Ampere Computing for about $6.5 billion.
notes: Full acquisition; Ampere is now a wholly owned subsidiary.

description: SoftBank signed an agreement to buy $2 billion of Intel common stock at $23 a share.
notes: Closing was not verified in the sources reviewed.

description: SoftBank owns about 86% of Arm, and a SoftBank affiliate supplied $704.4 million (14.3%) of Arm revenue in fiscal 2026.
source_publisher: TIKR, citing the Arm annual report
notes: disclosure_date is the Arm Form 20-F filing date. Related-party revenue rose from $145.5M a year earlier. SoftBank has pledged 769 million Arm shares for a margin loan reported at $25B, which helps fund its OpenAI investments (a-007).

description: ASML invested 1.3 billion euros (about $1.5 billion) in the Mistral AI Series C and became its largest shareholder with about 11%.
notes: Deal is in euros (EUR 1.3B); the USD figure is the approximate conversion used in press coverage.

description: Cerebras raised $5.55 billion in its May 2026 IPO at $185 a share, a fully diluted valuation of about $56.4 billion.
notes: Revenue is concentrated: G42 and MBZUAI were about 86% of 2025 revenue; OpenAI is the main new customer (a-019).
